messages:
elaine (CS): FYI customer (API-Team) reporting duplicate charges when clients reconnect to SSE streams. They see partial output, then a resumed chunk that repeats the last token and leads to duplicate generations and double billing.
API-Team (customer): repro steps: open SSE, get partial response, forcibly drop conn (tcp kill), then reconnect with resume_token. After reconnect we get the last ~5 tokens repeated and a new generation starts. Billing shows 2 generation charges.
API-Team (customer): minimal curl they used: 
```
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams?model=fast-16k&resume_token=abc123" -d $'prompt=Hello' 
```
API-Team (customer): logs show last-event-id: 98765 on client. On reconnect client sends resume_token=abc123 and last_event_id=98765. Server responds 200 and then sends data frames starting from seq 98765 again.
elaine (CS): attaching sanitized logs from customer (pushed to support bucket). Noticed the server emits event seq numbers but the first resumed frame repeats seq 98765 instead of 98766. Seems like an off-by-one resume window.
josh (eng-runtime): pinged. Can you paste the server-side chunk boundary logs? I want to see how we compute resume_start_seq vs acked_last_seq.
mina (eng-ml): possible cause: KV-cache snapshot used to seed continuation may be created at token boundary N, but resume offset applied inclusively instead of next token. That would re-emit token N.
API-Team (customer): timeout/latency pattern: drops usually at ~4s into stream; reconnect within 200-500ms. Not high concurrency. Happens reproducibly if reconnect happens within 1s of last chunk.
josh (eng-runtime): thanks. Quick triage: please capture two things from a repro run: 1) the last SSE "event: token_chunk" id/seq before disconnect; 2) the first SSE event after reconnect. If first_after_reconnect.seq == last_before_disconnect.seq then we repeated. If it equals last_before_disconnect.seq+1 then resume worked.
deploy-bot: deploy queued: runtime/patch/resume-boundary (priority: low) by josh.
josh (eng-runtime): hypothesis: resume_window calculation uses inclusive indices when it should be exclusive. Implement simple guard: if incoming.start_seq <= session.last_acked_seq then drop overlapping tokens (no-op) and advance resume pointer to session.last_acked_seq+1. Also emit metrics count.resume_overlap.
calvin (billing): if duplicate generation appears in the audit logs we can credit them, but need quick repro and exact request ids/time ranges. Please attach request ids for the two charged operations.
elaine (CS): provided request ids in support ticket #4321. Customer requests hotfix or workaround.
mina (eng-ml): longer term: add idempotency at generation level: generate_id derived from prompt+model+seed+generation_start_seq. If we see same generate_id twice, avoid charging 2x and dedupe response stream. Will need coordination with billing to retro-credit.
josh (eng-runtime): quick patch rolled to staging: if resume_start_seq <= last_ack_seq then set resume_start_seq = last_ack_seq + 1 and log debug: "adjusted_resume_start". Will push to prod after running canary.
elaine (CS): shared canary link with customer. They will test early tomorrow.
API-Team (customer): quick question — do you recommend client-side change too? We can add dedupe on client by ignoring first resumed event if seq == last_seen_seq.
josh (eng-runtime): yes please. Client-side dedupe is cheap and highly recommended: keep last_seen_seq and drop any incoming events with seq <= last_seen_seq. Also backoff before re-sending the original prompt; avoid re-submitting a fresh generation unless you detect explicit failure.
calvin (billing): action for billing: hold credits pending verification. I'll start an incident billing ticket and link audit logs.
mina (eng-ml): note: some models can non-deterministically re-tokenize boundaries when using quantized kernels; that could shift seq numbering by 1 in rare cases. Recommend adding a stable "generation_id" on server per session that survives reconnects.
elaine (CS): next steps: 1) eng-runtime implement prod guard + metric; 2) eng-ml add generation_id plan in RFC; 3) billing prepare provisional credit for support ticket #4321; 4) customer to test staging canary and verify duplicates gone.
josh (eng-runtime): I filed runtime issue: RH-1089 (resume off-by-one causing dupe tokens). Adding e2e unit that simulates socket drop and immediate resume.
API-Team (customer): testing now on staging canary — will report in ~30m. Thanks for quick triage. :pray:
elaine (CS): marking as escalated to eng-runtime + billing. I'll update ticket with canary results and next steps.
calvin (billing): thanks, looping in finance-ops for the potential credit flow.
deploy-bot: prod canary deploy scheduled 2024-02-21T16:12:00Z (josh).
mina (eng-ml): FYI if we add generation_id, we should include it in SSE frames as `x-gen-id` header/event so clients and billing can correlate.
josh (eng-runtime): agreed. I'll include x-gen-id in resumed frames.
elaine (CS): closing loop — customer confirmed duplicates gone on canary. Waiting for prod rollout. Will confirm after deploy. :thumbsup:
